subject: Velocis throughput spike — RCA packet and remediation verification
messages:
From: Alexandra Mendez <alexandra.mendez@velocis.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 09:12:10 -0700
Subject: Major degradation — high latency/5xx spike impacting inference

David —

We started seeing a sharp spike in tail latency and a concurrent rise in 5xx errors this morning around 08:45 PT. Customer-facing requests are timing out (p50 fine, p99 > 5s), and our order-processing pipeline is failing to get embeddings for a subset of traffic. Our engineers have uploaded a set of request traces and a log bundle (attached: velocis_logs_20280523.zip).

Key metrics observed:
- Error rate jumped from 0.2% -> 4.8% between 08:45–09:05 PT
- Tokenized throughput dropped ~35% on the main inference route
- P99 latency increased from ~1.2s -> ~5.4s

This is impacting checkout flows for multiple zones. We need an urgent bridge and an RCA delivered to our execs by EOD. Please escalate if you need leadership involvement.

—Alexandra
Alexandra Mendez
Head of Platform Ops, Velocis Corp.
attachments: velocis_logs_20280523.zip

Alexandra — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I'm on it and have looped in our incident lead (Neha) and the account steward (Grace). We're standing up a short technical bridge now to triage.

Immediate next steps:
- Neha will take triage and share an initial hypothesis within 2 hours.
- Grace will coordinate customer comms and keep your leadership updated.
- I'll own exec escalation and verify any SLA/credit needs.

I'll set a follow-up at 11:30 PT after the bridge.

—David

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 11:18:05 -0700
Subject: Preliminary findings — Velocis throughput spike

On Tue, May 23, 2028 at 09:26 AM David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alexandra — thanks for the heads up...

Quick triage summary from the bridge (10:00–11:00 PT):
- Observed pattern: sudden burst of high-concurrency requests with longer-than-usual prompt prefixes (~2.4x token length for a subset of traffic).
- Root trigger: our batching heuristic misclassified the incoming distribution which caused oversized batches on a subset of GPU workers, increasing queuing and causing KV cache churn.
- Secondary factor: a fallback quantized kernel path triggered for some model variants under high queue pressure; that path has higher variance and produced higher CPU-side deserialization latency.

Impact: elevated p99s and a transient rise in 5xx errors while workers recovered; throughput per-gpu dropped ~30% for ~12 minutes.

Short-term mitigations applied (10:30 PT):
- Reduced max batch size for affected workers (temporary safe floor).
- Forced routing away from the older quantized kernel for the primary model during the surge.
- Purged stale KV entries on impacted shards.

Next steps (owner / ETA):
- (Neha) Deep dive on batching heuristic and add traffic-shift detection + circuit breaker (ETA: 2028-05-30).
- (Grace) Customer comms + exec readout scheduling (ETA: 2028-05-24).
- (David) Confirm any contractual remedies & credits (ETA: 2028-05-25).

I'll prepare a concise RCA packet and recommended permanent fixes.

—Neha
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 10:02:05 -0700
Subject: Remediation plan and verification checklist — Velocis incident

Alexandra / Team —

Thanks for the bridge yesterday. Per our conversation, attached is the remediation plan and a short verification checklist. Link to working doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1VelocisRCA

Action items (condensed):
1) Batching heuristic hardening — add traffic-shift detector + automatic temporary batch size reduction (owner: Neha; ticket: SUP-4321; ETA: 2028-05-30)
2) Kernel-path stability work — audit quantized fallback path and add per-worker throttles (owner: infra-ml; ETA: 2028-06-14)
3) Customer-side observability hooks — add token-length alerting to Velocis ingestion pipeline (owner: Velocis; assistance: Grace; ETA: 2028-06-02)
4) Post-incident validation — staged load test and production canary (owner: Redwood QA; ETA: 2028-06-07)

Verification checklist for closure:
- Confirm SUP-4321 merged + deploy to staging
- Canary run for 48 hours w/ target load profile
- Week-by-week latency trend validated (p99 < 1.5s)

I'll host a brief exec readout on Friday 2028-05-26 10:00 PT unless you prefer a different slot.

Attachments referenced: action-tracker_velocis.csv

Best,
—Grace
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Mendez <alexandra.mendez@velocis.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 17:19:50 -0700
Subject: Velocis incident — RCA delivered and closure confirmation

Alexandra / Velocis execs —

Thank you all for patience while we completed the RCA and implemented the first wave of mitigations. Attached is the finalized RCA packet (rca_summary_velocis_20280530.pdf) and the action tracker (action-tracker_velocis.csv) showing items closed vs outstanding.

Summary:
- Root cause: batching heuristic + kernel fallback interaction under unexpected token-length distribution.
- Actions completed: temporary batch-size floor, routing changes, KV purge, SUP-4321 (traffic-shift detector) merged to main and deployed to staging.
- Outstanding: longer-term kernel-path audit and per-worker throttles (scheduled).

Remediation verification: our 48-hour canary completed with p99 latency back to baseline (target < 1.5s). We propose:
1) Closure of this incident upon acceptance of the RCA by Velocis execs.
2) A goodwill credit equal to 10% of May usage while the incident window was open (we will confirm with finance).
3) A follow-up exec readout next week to review long-term mitigations and timelines.

If accepted, we will mark the thread closed and move remaining engineering work into SUP-4321 and the kernel stability epic.

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
